# Ākaṅkheyya Sutta (MN 6 (PTS MN i 33))

**ID:** MN 6 (PTS MN i 33)
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Ākaṅkheyya Sutta
**PTS:** MN i 33
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0201m.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ākaṅkheyya Sutta* (MN 6) is the sixth discourse of the *Majjhimanikāya*, set at Sāvatthi in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park [Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995]. The discourse opens with the Buddha instructing monks to dwell accomplished in moral virtue, restrained by the disciplinary code (*pātimokkha-saṃvara-saṃvuta*), devoted to internal serenity, and dwelling in seclusion [Dutt 1924; Rogell 2003]. The Buddha presents ethical discipline and meditative cultivation as the indispensable foundation for fulfilling any spiritual desire or aspiration (*ākaṅkheyya*) [Rogell 2003]. These aspirations progress hierarchically from basic wishes—such as being loved and respected by fellow monastics or overcoming fear and anxiety in wilderness abodes—to mastering the four meditative absorptions (*jhāna*), acquiring supernormal powers and the six direct knowledges (*chalabhiññā*), and culminating in the destruction of the taints (*āsavakkhaya*) and awakening [Zhu 2017; Nyanaponika, Hecker & Bodhi 2003; Anālayo 2017; Melnikova 2014].

The sutta shares curated parallels with AN 10.71, AN 2.36, SN 47.46, and DN 2 (*Sāmaññaphala Sutta*) in the Pali canon, as well as MĀ 105 in the Chinese *Madhyamāgama* [Anālayo 2017]. A corresponding title (*agakṣaṇa*) is attested in a catalogue list of the Gāndhārī Senior Manuscripts [Allon 2014]. The sutta is also referenced in canonical and paracanonical works such as the *Vibhaṅga* and the *Milindapañha*.

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Full parallels: AN 10.71 Ākaṅkhasutta; MA 105 願
- Passage-level parallels: an2.36; DN 2 (PTS DN i 47) Sāmaññaphala Sutta; SN 47.46 Pātimokkhasaṁvarasutta
- Mentioned in: Mil 7.3.2 Padumaṅgapañha; Vb 12 Jhānavibhaṅga

**Sources**

- [Allon 2014] Mark Allon, Introduction: The Senior Manuscripts — Attestation of a parallel title 'agakṣaṇa' in the Gāndhārī Senior scroll list.
- [Zhu 2017] Tianshu Zhu, Buddhas and Bodhisattvas: Emanators and Emanated Beings in Buddhist Art of Gandhara, Central Asia, and China (2017) — Identification of the six supernormal knowledges (chalabhiññā) in MN 6 and parallels.
- [Dutt 1924] Sukumar Dutt, Early Buddhist Monachism (1924) — Discussion of the injunction on practicing sīla and being restrained under the Pātimokkha.
- [Nyanaponika, Hecker & Bodhi 2003] Nyanaponika Thera, Hellmuth Hecker, and Bhikkhu Bodhi, Great Disciples of the Buddha: Their Lives, Their Works, Their Legacy (2003) — Discussion of the five mundane superknowledges and divine eye as benefits arising from precept observance in MN 6.
- [Anālayo 2017] Bhikkhu Anālayo, A Meditator's Life of the Buddha (2017) — Note on absence of fear in secluded dwellings in MN 6 and its Madhyama-āgama parallel.
- [Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995] Bhikkhu Ñāṇamoli and Bhikkhu Bodhi, The Middle Length Discourses of the Buddha (1995) — Translation title, Sāvatthi setting, opening formula, and enumeration of mundane knowledges.
- [Melnikova 2014] Nora Melnikova, Modern School of Vipassana: A Buddhist Tradition (2014) — Note on the destruction of taints as culminating in liberation in MN 6.
- [Rogell 2003] Sharda Rogell, Pressing Out Pure Honey: A Practitioner's Study Guide (Majjhima Nikāya) (2003) — Summary of Buddha's exhortation to train in precepts, conduct, serenity, and insight.
